# SPAR — Behavioural Self-Signatures in LLMs

> Do LLMs leave recognisable behavioural signatures, and does a model have privileged access to its own? Part 1 (coin flips): a frozen 180-sequence corpus and eight experiments; no privileged self-recognition, and attribution follows the stated generation procedure. Part 2 (rock-paper-scissors and matching pennies, Astra/Fable/Qwen): telling a model its opponent's identity has no self-specific effect on play, and as observers only Fable predicts its own model better when labels are true. That effect is in cross-model games, is bounded by a history classifier, and sits near a judge-noise floor of ~80% test-retest agreement.

Start with the review guide. It gives the reading order, maps claims to evidence, indexes the runs, and lists large files to avoid.
